evidence: shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52 filters by query.expr then !query.hide; querySplitting.ts:296-299 filters !query.hide then query.expr. Both are pure, side-effect-free predicates, so the order doesn't change the result. The shard order also predates this PR (the old code chained .filter(expr).filter(!hide) after interpolateVariablesInQueries). Aligning the two is cosmetic.

The redundant pass is real: runShardSplitQuery interpolates at shardQuerySplitting.ts:52, then calls runSplitQuery at shardQuerySplitting.ts:163, which interpolates again at querySplitting.ts:299. But the claim overstates what is new. Every runQuery already goes through DataSourceWithBackend.query, which calls applyTemplateVariables again on each target (packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185). So before this PR the shard path already interpolated twice, through interpolateVariablesInQueries plus super.query, and the plain split path now does the same. Ad-hoc filters (datasource.ts:1127-1130 addAdHocFilters -> modifyQuery.ts:147 addLabelToQuery) and nested variable values were therefore already re-applied downstream. The PR adds one more pass of the same kind rather than a new failure mode. A skipInterpolation option would remove the extra work but is not needed for correctness relative to existing behavior.

shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:56-59: the beforeEach mock assigns query.expr = ... and returns the same object. The real LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables returns a new object via spread ({...target, expr, step, legendFormat}, datasource.ts:1135-1140), so the discrepancy is real. But it copies the pattern of the old interpolateVariablesInQueries mock this PR replaced, request is rebuilt per test in beforeEach, and the replacement is idempotent once $SELECTOR is gone, so no current assertion is masked. Returning {...query, expr: ...} is a cheap test-hygiene improvement.

shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:173-176: the 'Sends the whole stream selector' test overrides the mock with the same in-place mutation (query.expr = ...; return query). The real implementation returns a new object (datasource.ts:1135-1140). This is the same low-impact hygiene issue as id 2. It is inherited from the previous mock, and the test only asserts fetchLabelValues arguments, which don't depend on whether the object identity is preserved. Switching to a spread is optional.
